modalLead: A Jellyfin widget with the posters from your own library, a weekly digest of what needs you, and all of monitoring in one place: Config → Monitoring.

items.text: See what was added to your Jellyfin lately, with the real posters from your own library. Add the Jellyfin widget under Config → Widgets → Catalogue, fill in the address and an API key and press Connect. It shows a list, a strip with a tab per library, a grid, or the newest item large.
items.title: New in Jellyfin, with real posters

media.alt: The Jellyfin widget on the dashboard: posters of what was added lately, with the library under each

items.text: Config → Widgets has three tabs: Your widgets, Catalogue and Custom widget. The Catalogue shows every kind with a small picture of what it looks like, and the old Types tab folded into it. On a wide screen the list and the open widget stand side by side.
Renaming a widget no longer takes the cursor away when you move on to the next field.

Once a week, one message about what needs you: links that broke, certificates that run out soon, container updates, what you opened most, bookmarks nobody opens and what waits in the Inbox. It arrives as a push notification, through your alert service, and once as a card on the dashboard. A quiet week sends nothing.
items.title: One message a week about what needs you

media.alt: Config → Monitoring → Notifications, scrolled to the weekly digest

items.text: Read the digest opens a window with a part per subject and a button to the view where you deal with it. After a button it folds into a small bar in the corner that shows how far you are, with Next for the following part.
Pick the day, the hour and what goes in under Config → Monitoring → Notifications → Weekly digest. Send sends a proof digest right away. It is on by default, on Monday at 08:00.
The digest names the week's nextDash releases in a part called New in nextDash, with a button that opens this window. Switch the part off under Config → Monitoring → Notifications → Weekly digest.

Monitoring has its own section. Everything that was under Behavior → Status & alerts is now in Config → Monitoring, on three tabs: Checks, Notifications and Schedules for maintenance windows and quiet hours. Old links still land in the right place.
The tabs in a section stay on one row. On a narrow screen you scroll the row sideways instead of it breaking onto a second line.
A widget label you type right after Save is no longer wiped a moment later.
A release's highlight gets a spotlight at the top of this window: a picture or a short clip, a line of explanation and a button to where it lives.
Every release since your last visit opens here, with a count of what is new and fixed. Older releases stay folded under Earlier.
Paste a link and see what it is before you choose Add bookmark or Save to Inbox: the site's icon, title, a line about it and its picture.
The grip on a block can be dragged with the mouse again when the category headers use a style other than the theme's.
Clean up disk space says 1 stopped container and 1 image when there is only one.
Tag suggestions know a subdomain by its parent domain: docs.docker.com gets the tags of docker.com.
